title: Company priority tree and quarterly alignment playbook
creator: Ava Martínez
description:
Context: As Redwood scales, multiple product initiatives surface competing priorities at the company level. Currently, execs and initiative leads operate with slightly different success criteria and release horizons which produces tension during quarterly planning and ad-hoc escalations.

Goal: Deliver a concise, repeatable 'priority tree' and quarterly alignment playbook that: (1) maps company-level objectives to measurable initiative outcomes, (2) provides a lightweight decision rubric for trade-offs during quarter planning, and (3) standardizes cross-functional cadence (PM/Eng/Design/Sales/Customer Success) for escalation and rebalancing.

Scope: This ticket owns the playbook and lightweight templates (one-pager priority tree, escalation ladder, checklist for initiative intake) and a recommended cadence for the first two quarters of adoption. It does NOT change compensation frameworks or replace team-level roadmaps; it sits above those artifacts to improve cross-team decisioning.

Out-of-scope: Full org restructure, engineering sprint planning tooling changes, or mandatory gating on every minor initiative.

Why this matters: Clear, repeatable decisions at the company level reduce over-commitment, speed up resource reallocation when incidents or priority shifts occur, and reduce surprise scope pushes that harm SLOs or customer deliverables.
updates: 2026-03-11 - Initial draft of playbook completed. Shared with execs for feedback (see link). Highlighted need to codify 'initiative-class' buckets (strategic, growth, ops, reliability).
2026-03-12 - Feedback from CTO (Priya Singh): include acceptance criteria for 'critical reliability' initiatives and an explicit fast-path for incident-driven rebalancing.

2026-03-13 - Product leadership sync: recommend pilot with two initiatives from infra and two from product growth. Agreed owner list and weekly touchpoints. Action: PM to prepare intake template and one-pager by 2026-03-18.
2026-03-14 - Design reviewed one-pager, suggested a visual priority tree with color-coded risk vs impact axes. Design to hand off mock by 2026-03-17.
2026-03-15 - Engineering constraints doc (ENG-19742) linked; decision to include a matrix for capacity windows that maps to Dedicated/Private deployment release lanes. Need SRE sign-off before pilot.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page priority tree template exists and is usable by any initiative owner (template in Drive)
A 2-page playbook describing decision rubric, escalation ladder, and weekly alignment cadence is reviewed and approved by Exec (CEO & CTO)
Pilot roll-out plan with 4 initiatives, owners, and measurement plan (leading indicators + one lagging KPI per initiative)
Clear dependency map documented linking to engineering capacity constraints and risk windows (SRE + Infra approvals obtained)
At least two cross-functional rehearsals completed (mock planning sessions) and feedback incorporated
notes: Trade-offs discussed: tight gating improves focus but can slow emergent work. Playbook will include a 'fast-path' decision that allows bumping a high-severity customer or security issue through with SRE/CTO sign-off.
Proposed weekly cadence: 'Priority Stand' (15m) for initiative owners + monthly Exec alignment (45m). Include a quarterly retro to re-evaluate initiative-class boundaries.
Measurement: track number of mid-quarter scope additions, number of escalations, and percent of initiatives meeting planned milestone to quantify playbook impact after two quarters.
Stakeholders: Exec sponsor - CEO (Maya Thompson); PM lead - Ava Martínez; Eng sponsor - Priya Singh; Design - Miguel Chen; SRE - Lila O'Connor; Sales/CS rep - Thomas Nguyen.
